What RTA cabinets are

RTA stands for ready-to-assemble. The cabinets ship flat-packed in standard widths, and you, a handyman, or a contractor put the boxes together and install them. The price on the website usually covers the boxes and doors only.

[Owner: add what you see most often in RTA kits — box material, door options, typical issues after install.]

What custom means at PalmCraft

Custom cabinets are designed and built for one room. At PalmCraft, we measure your space for free, prepare a 3D design for your approval, and build the cabinets in our own Oldsmar shop with 3/4-inch plywood boxes. Our own team delivers and installs them.

Side by side

[Owner: check each line and add your own comparison points.]

  • Sizing: RTA comes in standard widths with filler strips to close gaps; custom is sized to your walls and appliances.
  • Design: with RTA you choose from a catalog; with custom you choose door style, material, color, and every handle.
  • Assembly and installation: RTA is assembled on site by you or a hired installer; PalmCraft cabinets arrive built and are installed by our team.
  • Warranty: RTA warranties usually cover the product, not the installation; PalmCraft gives a 24-month warranty on materials and craftsmanship.
  • Who you call if something is wrong: with RTA, the seller and the installer are often two different companies; with PalmCraft it is one team.

Compare the total cost, not the box price

An RTA quote and a custom quote rarely cover the same things. Before you compare, add assembly, installation, delivery, fillers and trim, and the design time to the RTA price.
